Fix GC of managed delegates passed across FFI boundary

When a managed callback is marshalled to unmanaged (via IntoUnmanaged()),
the native trampoline delegate backing the function pointer could be
garbage collected while Rust still held the raw pointer  causing:

  'A callback was made on a garbage collected delegate'

This happened because IntoUnmanaged() copied raw IntPtrs into the
Unmanaged struct but nothing kept the managed delegate alive. The
LibraryImport source-generated marshaller creates temporary callback
wrappers that become eligible for GC immediately after the P/Invoke.

Fix: IntoUnmanaged() now pins the callback instance via GCHandle and
passes a static destructor function pointer. When Rust drops the
callback, the destructor frees the GCHandle, allowing normal GC.

- Managed callbacks: GCHandle.Alloc(this) + static destructor
- Rust-originated callbacks: pass through _data/_destructor unchanged
- Add ServiceCallbacks.create_with_callback() + GC.Collect() test
- Revert service-level _prevent_gc (no longer needed)

fix(csharp): emit AsUnmanaged() on blittable slice bindings

The C# backend generates AsUnmanaged() calls for every composite field,
including slice fields, but the blittable-element slice template (fast.cs,
used for SliceByte/SliceU32/SliceVec3f32/...) only defined ToUnmanaged().
A struct embedding e.g. Slice<u8> therefore failed to compile with CS1061
(SliceByte does not contain a definition for AsUnmanaged).

Add AsUnmanaged() => ToUnmanaged() to fast.cs, mirroring the non-blittable
slice template (marshalling.cs) which already defines it. For a borrowed
slice the two are semantically identical.

Add a regression fixture (UseSliceByteInStruct { bytes: Slice<u8> } plus
pattern_ffi_slice_in_struct) to reference_project so the dotnet compile
gate exercises this path; previously no composite embedded a blittable slice,
which is why the broken codegen shipped uncaught.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Fix runtime racy shutdown on panic.

Fix racy Tokio shutdown using shutdown_background

The previous TokioInner::Drop spawned a detached, never-joined OS thread to
drop the runtime when in an async context. That detached thread races with
process/test-host teardown and could abort the .NET test host on Linux.

Use Runtime::shutdown_background() instead: it never blocks and is safe to
call from any context, including a Tokio worker thread, removing the need for
the spawned thread and the Handle::try_current() branch.
